I run Linux Mint mainly on all my personal machines, but have to run Windows for a few things. I got tired of having to run scripts, Microsoft performing updates to get around them and on and on. So, I switched to Server 2012 (available to me free as part of my company's MSDN subscription). Some things to consider:

  • Windows Server 2012 is made to run on production servers. As such, it comes bare-bones: No stupid forced (uninstallable) services, etc., etc.
  • You can configure it to look and act just like Windows 8.1...
  • There aren't any forced upgrades. Just general/security updates. But you choose when they get installed.
  • Without all the bloat (extra services, etc.), you'll get better performance overall. (Boot time, general application performance, etc.)
  • You can game on it just fine (I run Steam, have full drivers for my NVidia card / sound card, and everything works great.)

The downsides:

  • If you purchase it outright, it is 5x the cost of Windows 10. But, it may be worth it to you for all the shit Micro$oft is doing to Windows.
  • Sometimes driver installers fail because you are not Windows 7/8.1/10. But, this is easy to get around. I've found individual .EXE's in the subfolders that install the drivers just fine without performing an OS check.
If you must run Windows and are tired of the forced-upgrade cat-and-mouse game, consider running Server 2012 ...
